transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-22 10:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Singh - Redwood; Maya Chen, Ethan Rodriguez, Lena Park - Juno AI

00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, account exec. Quick intro, Priya is our SE, she'll handle the technical bits. Maya, over to you for quick context?
00:20 Maya Chen: Yeah hi, thanks. We're Juno AI, building a conversational routing layer for enterprise workflows, exploring embedding + generation flows. We're trying to scope whether Redwood's hosted API can get us to a working prototype fast, or we need dedicated capacity early.
00:40 Priya Singh: Great, quick clarifying question: when you say "protoype fast" do you mean like time-to-first-token for an engineer on your team, or performance at production QPS?
00:55 Maya Chen: Time-to-first-token first — we want our devs to experiment with free credits and integrate in a couple hours ideally. Then we'll run load tests to decide Dedicated.
01:15 Ethan Rodriguez: Yeah, the main constraints: we expect bursts to 200 qps for short periods, avg 20 qps; typical sequences 128 tokens for prompts, 256 for responses. Latency target is 200-400ms p50 for most user-facing calls. Cost is also a factor — we want lowest unit cost while hitting latency.
01:40 Priya Singh: That sounds doable. For PLG quickstarts we usually get engineers from sign-up to first token in under 30 minutes if they're using our SDK + quickstart repo. There's a free credits program that activates on sign-up, we can send that link.
01:55 Jordan Lee: I'll follow up with the credits link and a one-click quickstart doc. There was also a note about SDK; we support Python, Node, and cURL examples.
02:10 Maya Chen: Perfect. A few security questions up front — do you have SOC2? Can we do customer-managed KMS for keys? And VPC/private deployment options?
02:30 Lena Park: Yeah sec team s here — we need to know about audit logs, data retention, and whether payloads can be restricted to our region.
02:45 Priya Singh: Short answers: Redwood is SOC2 compliant (we'll share the cert), we support KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private deployments and we have a Private option for air-gapped / VPC, but hosted API is Redwood-managed KMS by default. Audit logs and per-request tracing are available in the Console. We'll send the security pack after the call.
03:10 Maya Chen: Good. When would you recommend Dedicated vs Hosted for us? Our main worry is the 200 qps bursts and data residency.
03:25 Priya Singh: Hosted is easiest for PLG and early POC — it's fast to get started, low friction, and you get free credits. If you need consistently high throughput or customer-managed KMS/VPC, Dedicated is the next step; Private for fully air-gapped or on-prem. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable latency.
03:45 Ethan Rodriguez: On Dedicated, how do you handle autoscaling and burst capacity? Our traffic is spiky — bursts 10x base for short times.
04:00 Priya Singh: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity options. We typically recommend a small reserved footprint plus burst capacity for spikes. Also caching and prefix KV cache can reduce backend QPS significantly for repeated prompts.
04:30 Jordan Lee: Also to manage cost we can suggest quantized model variants or smaller models for non-latency-critical paths. We'll include model recommendations in the POC sizing.
05:00 Maya Chen: Sounds good. Can you give an example of time-to-first-token flow? For our devs to get an API key and run a sample request.
05:20 Priya Singh: Sure example flow: sign up -> get free credits activated -> create API key in Console -> run npm install @redwood/inference -> run sample script which calls Redwood.chat.complete or Redwood.generate -> first token arrives in <500ms on hosted for small sequences; in practice devs get first responses within minutes. We'll send a one-file example.
05:50 Ethan Rodriguez: There are some model specific questions — we use embeddings for retrieval and a small LLM for reranking. Do you provide an embeddings endpoint and rerank recipe?
06:10 Priya Singh: Yes we have embeddings API and you can use our rerank endpoint or do a custom rerank flow. We also have verified model performance profiles in the catalog. We'll share the catalog link.
06:30 Lena Park: Regarding logs and PII, if we route customer data through hosted, is there retention or deletion controls? We're GDPR sensitive.
06:45 Priya Singh: Hosted has data retention settings and you can request deletion; for strict residency and retention controls we recommend Dedicated or Private where you can control retention more tightly and optionally use customer-managed KMS.
07:05 Jordan Lee: Quick qualification question — what's your timeline and decision process?
07:15 Maya Chen: Timeline: want a POC in the next 4 weeks, decide by end of Q4. Decision makers: Myself + CTO, infra team for security sign-off (Lena), and procurement later. Success criteria: 1) devs can integrate and hit first token quickly, 2) latency within SLA for 95% of calls under target, 3) cost per token within our budget envelope.
07:45 Priya Singh: Good. For the POC we typically provision a small hosted account and run a production-like load test; if performance/cost doesn't meet SLOs, we size a Dedicated cluster for you.
08:10 Ethan Rodriguez: What's the expected unit cost differences between hosted and dedicated? Ballpark numbers are fine.
08:25 Jordan Lee: Ballpark — hosted has pay-as-you-go rates; Dedicated can reduce unit cost by ~20-40% depending on utilization because of reserved capacity and batching/CPU optimizations. We'll send a pricing tiers doc with examples for your sequence lengths.
08:55 Maya Chen: For the dev quickstart, can you include a runnable notebook with embedding + retrieval + rerank example?
09:10 Priya Singh: Yes, we have a Quickstart repo with notebooks. I'll attach the specific notebook for embedding + retrieval + rerank.
09:30 Lena Park: A note on compliance: we need SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs for pilot. Is SSO supported?
09:45 Priya Singh: SAML SSO is supported for Dedicated and Private; for hosted we offer SSO for higher tiers — we'll include detail in the security pack. RBAC and audit logs are in the Console.
10:05 Ethan Rodriguez: A couple of micro questions on batching: how do you control batching vs latency? We can't afford large batch waits for interactive calls.
10:20 Priya Singh: Our runtime uses continuous batching with latency SLOs. You can configure per-route latency targets, and the runtime will trade off batching to meet latency. For interactive paths we recommend smaller batch sizes or lower batch windows. We'll include recommended defaults.
10:45 Jordan Lee: Any obvious blockers from your side for trying hosted quickstart?
10:55 Maya Chen: No blockers — main asks are the quickstart + credits, security docs, and a POC sizing proposal.
11:10 Priya Singh: We'll also need your traffic profile (peak qps, avg seq len) to size the POC; Ethan if you can share that, Priya will put a sizing doc together.
11:30 Ethan Rodriguez: I'll pull logs and share a synthetic profile — expect that by end of week.
11:45 Jordan Lee: Awesome. Recap: Jordan send credits + quickstart, Priya send SDK snippets, POC sizing, and security pack. Customer to share traffic profile and security questions. We'll schedule a follow-up technical deep dive next week.
12:00 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, looking forward to the quickstart.
12:05 Jordan Lee: Thanks all, bye.

Notes on transcript quality: some names and acronyms auto-transcribed (e.g., "KV cache" as "K V cache"), minor mis-hearings present.

End transcript.
